name: Flip a coin across your fingers
blurb: The knuckle roll: a coin walks across the back of your fingers, tumbles into your thumb and returns. Pure fidget-level practice, permanently impressive.
gear: A large, thick coin — half dollar, £2, €2
steps: Balance the coin on the edge of your index finger, held vertically by your thumb.
Tip it over the index finger so it lands on top of the gap between index and middle.
Lift the middle finger to flip the coin over onto the next gap, and repeat across all four fingers.
Once at the little finger, drop the coin into the thumb underneath and return it to the start position.
Chain the whole cycle continuously, working towards a slow, even rhythm.
Practise on both hands and while looking away.
tips: Keep your hand fairly flat and level; tilting it drops the coin every time.
Do it over a table or your lap or you will spend the fortnight crawling on the floor.
proof: Five continuous cycles across the fingers and back through the thumb, without a drop.
